decisions.reason: After Product B was removed, this earmold is the more likely survivor in the hearing-care range, so its fit with the core business now outweighs the still modest visibility risk.
This thermoforming unit supports the firm's established laboratory workflows and remains a well-aligned equipment product in a growing market, making withdrawal unlikely absent clearly weak sales.

The orthopedic shoe last is the least natural fit with the firm's main dental and hearing focus, but its dedicated presentation and transferable digital-manufacturing know-how justify keeping it on the market for further validation.
A post-curing unit fits the firm's push into digital and automated production, so despite its newer and less prominent market presence it is likely to be retained as a complementary system product.
